text: Chapter 2, "Volume Two: Do Not Name That Chord," is a comprehensive reference catalog rather than instructional text, spanning pages 190-378 and presenting systematic voicing tables organized by sonority type and harmonic context. The chapter methodically catalogs 3-part and 4-part quartal voicings (close, spread, and cluster formations) across six cycles (cycles 2-7) and three parent scales (C Major, C Melodic Minor, and C Harmonic Minor), marking the volume’s strategic shift away from tertian harmony toward quartal and cluster sonorities that resist conventional chord naming. Each voicing entry provides three essential mappings: Intervallic Voice-Leading (pitch relationships), Functional Voice-Leading (harmonic context), and an M.S.R.P. string indicating the Most Stepwise Resolution Pattern available to that voicing. With no instructional prose, the chapter functions as a lookup resource for guitarists seeking to understand how non-tertian sonorities behave across different harmonic environments and voice-leading constraints. The catalog’s organization by voicing type, scale source, and resolution pattern enables rapid cross-reference for composition, improvisation, or harmonic analysis work grounded in quartal rather than tertian logic.
